utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We're proceeding with a new witness. The Prosecution. Can the usher please assist the witness to take the solemn declaration. Good afternoon. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, Kemal Mehinovic, solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. The Prosecution. Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I just advise the Bench of something before I commence with my examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This witness, as I think is indicated in his 65 ter summary, will speak about all of the defendants but particular acts of three of the defendants; one defendant who -- is Mr. Simic, who is currently in the detention facility. It is likely that -- well, Mr. -- the witness will be providing the Chamber with evidence about Mr. Simic this afternoon. And I've consulted with the Defence counsel about any matters pertaining to identification, and what Defence counsel have done is undertake that they will consult with their client during the break. And should the defendant have any concerns about identification issues, then he will advise the Prosecution and the Bench after how we would resolve that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could I ask you to state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Kemal Mehinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I understand it's your birthday today, is it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Happy birthday. How old are you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Forty-six.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you grow up and spend most of your life in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you get married in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And have children in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many children do you have, Mr. Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And are they girls, boys?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: A son and a daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you were all living together in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have a nickname when you were living in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Kemal Pekar, which means "the baker."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why did you have the nickname "the baker"?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Because that's what I do for a living.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was that a family business?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your father had been a baker in Bosanski Samac before you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you just a baker or did you have other business interests in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I also worked in various companies and I owned a restaurant together with my brother; in fact, two restaurants.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What were the names of the companies you worked in?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: The first was Mlinpak and the other company was Mebos.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When did you stop working in these companies?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after that I take it you concentrated on the bakery and the restaurants?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you're a Bosnian Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And so is your wife?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you were living in Bosanski Samac, did you get on well with your other neighbours who weren't from the same ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did members of all ethnic groups visit your restaurant, buy bread from your bakery?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you complete your compulsory service with the JNA when you were still living in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after you finished your compulsory service, did you continue to go back for updated training courses?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, after the end of the Communist Party in the former Yugoslavia, did you join any of the new political parties which began to emerge?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I did. The SDP party.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Whilst you were living in Bosanski Samac, did you ever own any weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of a hunting club? Did you own a hunting rifle or anything innocuous like that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You never at any stage had, either legally or illegally, held weapons in your house or any of your business premises?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'd like to ask you about some people from Bosanski Samac. Do you know someone called Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber how you know Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagoje Simic was, at the time when we met, a general practitioner in Bosanski Samac. We were assigned to the same unit at military drills, in which we took part together, so we knew each other rather well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: These military drills, are they these compulsory refresher courses that you said you used to attend?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Mehinovic, in fact it would be correct to say that both you and Mr. Simic were members of the JNA reserves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, could you assist the Chamber, and if you see Mr. Blagoje Simic here today, could you tell the Chamber where he is.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's sitting in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could the record reflect that Mr. Blagoje Simic has been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you know someone else by the name of Simic, but this time a Mr. Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And again, could you tell us how well you would have known Mr. Simic, Mr. Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I've known him for a pretty long time. He's younger than me. I know his father rather well. He worked in the municipality, his father, I mean, and it was from him that I got approvals, such as for building my house or the building where my business was located, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Miroslav Tadic, I take it you know him too?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a very good friend of my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, could you assist the Chamber and tell them if you see him here today and where he is.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's sitting to my left and to the right of Mr. Blagoje.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the record could reflect that Mr. Tadic has been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Mr. Simo Zaric, if you know him again could you just tell the Chamber again how you know him and again if you see him here today.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know him rather well. I've known him since early childhood. Mr. Simo Zaric was chief of the SUP for a while, that is, chief of police, and he went on to other jobs later. I know him from cultural society, the folk songs section.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Mehinovic, to complete the record could you tell the Chamber if you see Mr. Zaric here today.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And just explain where he's sitting.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: He's sitting to the left of Mr. Blagoje Simic, the first in the row.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, the final identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'm going to ask you now about the time period 1992 and particularly March and April 1992. I'd like to know whether you experienced or witnessed a rise in the interethnic tensions in Bosanski Samac in around this period.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you just give us one brief example of how these ethnic tensions showed themselves or manifested themselves.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't quite understand. Do you mean before the war? In the month of March?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Mehinovic. Yes, exactly, in March. In around March.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: It was at the time when barricades and roadblocks were put up. We didn't want to have trouble with any political parties. We wanted to continue living together as good friends. I had a good friend by the name of Danilo. I forget his last name. And he advised me to approach Mr. Miroslav Tadic to get security for my restaurant, and he also suggested I should join the 4th Detachment, the so-called 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, is the Mr. Miroslav Tadic you're talking about now the same one you identified in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did this Danilo advise you to go to Mr. Tadic to get security for your restaurant?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was a group that was planned by them to handle the defence of the town of Samac, but I don't know who they were supposed to defend it from.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, when you say "it was a group," are you talking now about the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So did Mr. Danilo tell you that if you want -- that you should join the 4th Detachment and you should do that by going to Mr. Tadic's restaurant?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Danilo tell you that if you went there, you'd be issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you go to Mr. Tadic's restaurant and try to procure a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you see other people in around Bosanski Samac at this time who had joined the 4th Detachment? Did you know of people who joined the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was Muharem Hatic, nicknamed Hanko, who was a good friend of mine, and Danilo too. That's one of many such men.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did these men who were members of the 4th Detachment carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would they be walking around Bosanski Samac with these weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On numerous occasions, they walked dressed in civilian clothes with weapons hidden under their jackets. They would move around town and in certain places around the mosque where you could frequently see the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But these men who you said were dressed in civilian clothing and with weapons in their jackets, these were people you knew to be members of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you have any information from any of these people as to whether or not they received payment for being a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mehinovic, you've given evidence that there was a rise in, I think, tension, including some barricades being set up. Did you yourself participate in any barricades or patrols or anything like that that was going on in Bosanski Samac in the months preceding April 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was indeed a barricade put up near the Mebos factory, but I wasn't involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you partake in any patrols going around the -- going around Bosanski Samac at the time?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You've testified that you were a member of the SDP. Were you politically -- were you particularly politically active, or were you simply a member on the books?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: After the disintegration of Yugoslavia, you were supposed to join in some of the new parties, so I chose the SDP. And I was a rank in file member, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Simo Zaric a member of the SDP?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I wasn't that well informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, then, that up until the 17th of April, 1992 that you basically ran your businesses, minded your own business, and were not in any way politically engaged or active?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'm going to ask you now about the night of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. I take it that -- on the night of the 16th and 17th of April, were you at home with your family?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And were you woken at some stage during the night by gunfire?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. It was around 3.00 in the morning. I was awoken by rifle fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you react when you heard -- how did you react when you heard this rifle fire?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: First I went to the window to see what the problem was, what was going on. When I turned my eyes towards the department store, I saw masked soldiers shooting to the left of the department store, and I retreated from the window immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you said when you looked out your window, you turned towards the department store. Do I take it that your house is pretty much in the centre, then, of Bosanski Samac town?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you had witnessed these masked soldiers outside and retreated from the window, when was the next time that you looked outside to see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning around 6.00 a.m., it became quiet, there was no more shooting, and I set out towards my restaurant. After a while, my brother dropped in and told me, "What's the matter with you? Don't you see there's a war going on? Go back to your home immediately."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, the flat you're talking about and the restaurant, are they close together?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't the bakery. The bakery was in a new neighbourhood close to the stadium, in the house owned by Srecko Ivic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, so that I'm clear, at 6.00 when you set out, was it towards your restaurant, then, or towards the bakery?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the bakery.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. So after your brother had warned you, did you actually return home?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, when was the next time that you left your apartment on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: It was at 8.00, perhaps 8.30, if I remember well. To the right of my house, from the direction of the retirees' home, a group of men in civilian clothes was moving: Ibrahim Salkic, Hasan Bicic, and another Bicic. I don't know all the names, but I knew all these people. When I went out to meet them, I asked them what was the matter, and they told me that there was a massacre of citizens in Donja Mahala going on and they were going to defend them. I accompanied them almost up to the school, which is right after the department store when you turn into Stjepan Radic Street. There we were intercepted by Dujmusic, and he talked them out of going there, telling them that they would all get killed and that they should go back. On our way back, we passed by the restaurant between the department store and the artesian well, and we assembled there in the yard of the so-called Carrington building. In that yard, Muhamed, nicknamed Biber, came out and talked with Mr. Ibela Salkic, who had a radio transmitter on him. They went to his flat, and on the way back from his flat, Salkic said that he had talked to Mr. Nikolic and said that the army would come and handle all the problems, that we shouldn't get involved any further and we should go home instead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, this Mr. Nikolic you said that -- the Mr. Nikolic with whom Ibalo Salkic made contact, was that Lieutenant Colonel Stefan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you got the instructions that you should all go home, did you then return home?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We all left in the same direction. I went with Kemal Atic, nicknamed Kilo. We were walking towards my house, which is the second street from there, the Vuk Karadzic Street. I walked Kemal to his home because he was very sickly at the time, and that's about all we did. The whole time we were outdoors.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Whilst you were outdoors and with the people you've just advised the Chamber about, did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you armed at any stage whilst you were outside of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you returned home, could you tell us the next thing that happened to you, still this morning of the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed home. I didn't go out any more. And then there was a transportation vehicle that was saying through the megaphone that whoever had weapons should bring the weapons outside of the house and that nothing would happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did anyone approach your home and ask you whether or not you had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: This was in the dusk, before the evening. Mr. Dragan Borojevic came with two soldiers and asked if there was anything there, and he said that he knew this house and he believed that there were no weapons here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, over the next few days, did you receive information from the authorities by way of loudspeaker announcements?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received information that those people that had reserve military uniforms should be at 10.00 in front of Buducnost.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you go to the Buducnost factory then?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took my reserve uniform and went to Buducnost, where we were greeted by Savic, Jovo Savic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, as best as you can remember, was this the next day, the 18th of April, or a day or so after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was the 18th or the 19th, up to the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there a few of you gathered there in front of the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There was maybe, in my estimate, about 40 to 50 people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: These 40 to 50 people, and not including Mr. Jovo Savic, what was the ethnic background of these people?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims and Croatians.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were these people wearing white armbands at the time?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had to wear a white armband on our left arm so that we could be recognised who we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How did you know that you had to wear these white armbands?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: On the same day that was declared, when we returned the reservist uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's when you heard. And how did you hear that you should be wearing a white armband to distinguish yourself? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Through the loudspeaker that was -- there was a jeep that had a loudspeaker, and that jeep was giving these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: From your observation at the Buducnost factory, was it only people of Muslim and Croat background who were wearing these white armbands?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What did Mr. Savic say to the people who were gathered there that morning?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: The majority of the people required the security of their houses and their streets. We were told to go to Cafe AS, to Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did Mr. Savic tell you why you should go to Miroslav Tadic's Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't -- I'm not familiar with that. I was a little bit further away from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But you're certain that you heard instructions that you were to go to Miroslav Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you go to Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why didn't you go to Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't consider it important for me to have any kind of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So again, it was your understanding that Mr. Savic was telling you to go to Mr. Tadic's cafe if you wanted to join in the security detail; is that it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you were told by a loudspeaker that you should wear a white armband when you venture out to identify yourself. Over the loudspeaker did you hear any other restrictions imposed on the Muslim and Croat communities?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that more than three Muslims could not move together in the city, in the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you given any explanation as to why that should be, or were you simply advised that no more than three Muslim -- or three Muslims or more should not move about publicly in the town?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: There was no explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, in the days following the takeover, did you ever receive any order to present yourself for labour assignment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked to report. I think it was forced labour and not a labour service. We were supposed to call -- to go to the Secretariat of National Defence and to report to Ljubo Borojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how did you receive this instruction that you were to go to the Secretariat of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Certain couriers went there from home to home, and they were distributing invitations and they were also orally informing people that they were on the list and that they should report to Borojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you obey the instructions to report to the Secretariat of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, could you assist us by telling us approximately how many days after the takeover this occurred.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I received the request to report around the 24th to the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you reported to the Secretariat of National Defence, could you tell us what happened that morning.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I reported to Borojevic, and he told me to wait, that I would go with a group of people to build bunkers in Pisare and that I would also dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm for us where exactly did you report to this Mr. Borojevic.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: At that time that was the Secretariat for National Defence close to the old bank, the SDK in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you the only one who turned up that morning, or were there more people who turned up for, as you said, forced labour?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was more people with me there. At that point, there were maybe 15 to 20 people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the people who were with you that morning, did you -- could you tell us about the ethnic background of them -- what their ethnic background was.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were there any of the Serb population who turned up for forced labour?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were all of the Muslims and Croats assembled there wearing their white armbands?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you were told you would go with a group of people to build bunkers in Pisare. Is Pisare a village in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And could you describe for the Chamber what this task of digging trenches involved, how you were taken there and what you did when you actually reached Pisare.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: We went on foot with a group leader. It was very close, this place where we were supposed to dig trenches. This is a demarcation line on the River Bosna, the line between Croats and the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And these trenches that you were to dig, did this place you between the Croats and the Serbian army when you were digging the trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: These trenches were actually fortifications of the lines. We were by the Serb army, not between, and we were fortifying the lines where the soldiers would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was there firing going on whilst you were digging these trenches or fortifying the lines?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was -- there was firing. There was sniper fire as well against us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was anyone injured by the sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: While I was there, I didn't see anybody getting injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The people who were digging these trenches, were they only Muslims and Croats or were any of the Serbs made to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. In my group, there were only Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Whilst you were digging these trenches, were you guarded by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So could you have left of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were the soldiers armed whilst they were guarding you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you want to dig these trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How did you feel whilst you were being made to dig these trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I felt humiliated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why humiliated, Mr. Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I think that -- I don't think there was any need for me to do forced labour and then not to mention that there was also people with a gun standing just above me. I think that can only be seen as humiliation. And they were also firing over our heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did this firing and the sniper fire, did it scare you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Roughly how many days were you digging trenches on these lines in Pisare?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: From the 24th until the closure every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say "until the closure," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Till I was taken to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mehinovic, I'd just like to concentrate now on Pisare, because I understand that you didn't spend all your time digging trenches in that location. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I might have been in Pisare two to three days. Later I was transferred to the embankment between Prud and Bosanski Samac, in the direction from the bridge to the Vijenac JNA Street. In that area, I made bunkers and my commander was Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a clean copy of a map which is currently in evidence as Prosecution Exhibit P9. I've shown this clean version to Defence counsel. And what I'd just ask the witness to do is just to briefly mark the location on this map just where he was digging these trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, there is going to be a map placed on the ELMO beside you. If you can have a look at the map and orientate yourself. Could you mark with an "X" and then write a number "1" beside the location where you were digging trenches. I think you'll -- these are the trenches you've just described now to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. Mehinovic, you could just put a number "1" beside that in case there are further additions -- further markings made on this map, just a number "1."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, Mr. Mehinovic has put three X's on the map, 1, 2, and 3, and they all depict the line where he was digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, just to confirm, the X's you've marked, this is the place where you were guarded by Mr. Radovan Antic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And it's the location where you dug trenches up until your arrest after the first two or three days in Pisare.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: MS. REIDY: Thank you. I'm finished with the map for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have a number for it, please, an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be P9J. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you've told us about being guarded by Radovan Antic. How well did you know Radovan Antic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Quite well, because he was my teacher in primary school. Also, we were -- he was the commander of both me and Mr. Blagojevic in the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you talk to any of the other guards who were with you whilst you were digging trenches during this -- this month or so?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Antic or anyone else ever mention Mr. Simo Zaric or Mr. Miroslav Tadic to you whilst you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, in this second location which you just marked on the map, as in Pisare, were you also exposed to sniper fire and crossfire between opposing factions?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you also guarded by armed soldiers while you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was this digging of trenches and bunkers, was this tough physical labour?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had to carry concrete slabs from two metres wide and one metre long, and we had to place them in whenever Antic would tell us, face towards the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In your JNA service, in your military service, had this been a specialisation of yours: digging trenches, building bunkers?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was there any reason why you should be assigned this task?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any payment for the work you carried out on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you receive any payment in kind, food for your family or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you get days off? You worked Monday to Friday or did you work every day until you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I worked every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Mehinovic, did you feel you had any choice whatsoever in carrying out these assignments?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: During this month while you were working and digging trenches and building bunkers, did you hear of other people doing a similar task to you being injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. While I was -- while I had this assignment, I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you hear about it when you didn't have this assignment? Did you hear of such things happening to other people who had similar assignments?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Before I was arrested, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do I understand that after you were arrested you heard of people who had been injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were these people who had been injured or killed whilst digging trenches and building bunkers?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic background of those people who were injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I do. Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you know of the relationship between Mr. Radovan Antic and either Mr. Simo Zaric or Mr. Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you said that you continued this sort of forced labour until the closure, until you were arrested and taken to the police station. What day was this, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: My being taken to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It was May 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where were you arrested from?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I was arrested in my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, I have a still from a video, which was a video disclosed to the Defence, and it's a still which -- in effect, a photograph from the video which I'd just like to put to the witness for identification. And these were shown earlier to Defence counsel, and I believe they have no objection to its being used and entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask for that still just to be put on the ELMO so the defendants can also see the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, could you tell us what that building in the photograph is?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: That is my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And downstairs we can see an establishment with a red or pink awning. Is that also belonging to you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: The left side belongs to me. The right side belongs to my brother. This shop here belongs to me. This other one belongs to my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So you and your brother own those two establishments and your house is upstairs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how many houses or apartments are above the restaurants and businesses?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: There were two above, and there was a third behind the restaurants, behind the establishments.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was this the building where you were arrested -- from where you were arrested on the 27th of May?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I ask that this be entered into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please. Can we have an exhibit number for it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be Exhibit P53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. That can be removed from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, how many people came to arrest you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Two came up the stairs leading to my home and another two were waiting outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the two who came upstairs, did you know them?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know them. They were Zoran Palezica and a man named Radulovic. Mr. Radulovic used to be a policeman in Zagreb before the war, and he came to Bosanski Samac during the war. I believe he is originally from Skarici village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And when these men came upstairs, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: They wanted me to come with them and give a statement at the Bosanski Samac police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell you what the statement would be about?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell me anything at all. They just told me to get moving, and they started beating me even while I was climbing down the stairs, in plain sight of my wife and children and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What were they beating you with in front of your wife and children and mother?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: They beat me with a police truncheon, they kicked me, they also beat me with a knuckleduster.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they use any insults against you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What sort of insults?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: They cursed my balija mother and they said something like, "How could you ever have thought that you would be -- you would kill me?"

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I take it that -- I'm correct in saying that the term "balija mother," that is an insulting term against Muslims, is it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell your wife or children or mother how long you would be giving this statement or when they could expect to see you back?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When they had taken you downstairs, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: They pushed me into a green Lada and then they took me directly to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The green Lada was a civilian car, was it, not a police car?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a civilian car.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what happened when they took you to the police station?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I was brought to the officer on duty, where I had to empty my pockets of all my possessions: my papers, my -- take off my watch, take off my shoelaces. And while I was handing over my documents, Nikola Vukovic happened to come by, and he told me, "Here's another birdie coming in. I have no time to talk to you now. We'll see each other. We'll be seeing each other." After that, I was taken to the so-called intake room. In that room, there was a man named Goran who, as far as I know, was a bodyguard of Stevo Todorovic. He gave me a piece of paper on which to write my statement and instructed me to use the Cyrillic script and to put in my statement the whereabouts of Mr. Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, could I just interrupt you there. I'd just like to ask you one or two more questions about the testimony you've already given.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you had to take -- when you had to hand over all your possessions, did you have to sign a receipt for them or did you get any acknowledgment that they'd been taken from you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't sign anything, nor did I get anything from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This Mr. Nikola Vukovic that you've mentioned, you knew him before this meeting in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when you met him this time, was he in civilian clothes or was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you see whether he was armed or not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was armed. He had a pistol on him. I believe it was a Colt.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You then testified that you were taken to what I believe you said was an intake room, or perhaps a reception room would be another wording.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were there other detainees in that room when you first arrived, or at the very beginning of your detention were you by yourself?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Approximately how long were you by yourself in that room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I was there perhaps an hour maybe, an hour and a half, two.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, I know you've testified that you were visited by a man called Goran. But beyond police officers, at any stage did they bring in any other detainees to join you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. There was Nijaz Alatovic, Kemal Kulugic, Hamed Sukur, and a man by the last name of Coralic, nicknamed Brica or "barber."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So at some stage there were about five of you in that room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: All of you, were you Muslim or Croat?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: We were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You were Muslims. Do you know where these other four men had come from? Had they been detained somewhere else, or were they just newly arrested like you too? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe they were brought from the town. I don't think they had been detained before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you know this person Nijaz Alatovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's a relative of my wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did he say anything to you while you were detained about helping you get released?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He talked to me in particular and told me that he was good friends with Mr. Simo Zaric. He said, "I'll go and talk to him, and I'll make inquiries about you too."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Nijaz said that he'd approach Mr. Zaric about having you released; is that it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What happened to the five of you in that room? Did you stay in that room for the rest of the day, or were some of you taken out?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. After a while, the officer on duty came and started calling out names. The first to be called out was Nijaz Alatovic, and we could hear the guard saying distinctly, "Simo Zaric is expecting you." So Nijaz went there. And when the interview was over, in view of the fact that this -- the window of this room is overlooking the street, we could see Nijaz going towards his home. After him, Sukur, Kulugic, and the barber left, and I couldn't see them through the window because they had to turn left. And I thought that since they hadn't come back to the room, they must have been released too. While this -- these interviews, these four interviews took place, the door of my room was open, and Mr. Simo Zaric would go down and tell the officer on duty, "Go on with the beating."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you said that the door of your room was open. Does this mean that whilst you were in the room that you could sometimes see Mr. Simo Zaric out in the corridor or somewhere else outside of the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, only in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Only in what sense, Mr. Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I mean that it was the only moment when I saw him, when we came down from his office to that hallway. And that was the single moment when I was sitting in the left corner of the room and the door was slightly ajar at an angle at which I could see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'm just going to ask you some questions about this because it's just important for the record that your experience is clear. So you have testified that the other people detained with you were taken out for what you understood to be a -- some form of interrogation. Does that mean that they were all taken out and at some stage you were left alone again in the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were taken out from that room where I was. They were taken to the office of Mr. Zaric, and I was left alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I understand that you yourself -- were you taken up to Mr. Simo Zaric's office?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But at some stage you saw Mr. Simo Zaric in the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you could see him from the room where you were now alone in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Are you sure that it was Mr. Simo Zaric who you saw in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall whether Mr. Zaric was in civilian clothes or wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: He was in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall whether he was armed or not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had a Skorpion gun on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric actually enter your room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But you heard -- you testified that you heard Mr. Zaric say something; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that I was in for a beating. In fact, he said something to that effect to the officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So you could see him outside your room talking to another police officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you actually hear Mr. Zaric say that you should be beaten?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And can you be certain that it was Mr. Zaric's voice you heard?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric have a very distinctive voice?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zaric looking in your direction when he said that you should be beaten?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the duty officer actually come in and beat you at that time?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was Mr. Stevan Todorovic who came later, together with his bodyguard, Goran; Slobodan Jakupovic, nicknamed Zvarka; Stojan Kojic, also known as Sole, and that group started to beat me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This Goran, this is the person you mentioned earlier in your testimony who you said wanted you to write a statement in Cyrillic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So did Mr. Goran come into your room twice, then; once to ask you for the statement and once in the company of the persons you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came in twice, and that was the second time. First he wanted from me that statement indicating the whereabouts of Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you able to provide him with the information about Mr. Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you know where Mr. Fitozovic was?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I know the man, but I didn't know where he was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What happened to you when you were unable to produce the Cyrillic statement Mr. Goran was looking for?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when Goran saw that the paper was blank, he and Todorovic started to beat me. They hit me with a truncheon, with a baseball bat, with a bar that was lying behind the cupboard. It was a metal bar. And I think they beat me for an hour, an hour and a half, maybe two hours. I'm not sure any longer. And then they took a break. After that break, they brought another three young men from the TO, the Territorial Defence. Those three men were Hasan Hadzialijagic; Admir Dzakic; and Srna, nicknamed Cuba. Right after they had come, they resumed beating both me and them, and that lasted for a rather long time. When the beating was over - it must have been after midnight, 1.00 or 2.00 a.m. - the three men were taken away. They were taken back to the TO building, and I stayed behind in that room.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. These three men, Mr. Hadzialijagic, Mr. Dzakic, and Cuba --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Madam Prosecutor. When you are talking about beating with baseball bats and whatever, what kind of beating was it? Did they hit you on your head or arms, or which part of the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They beat me all over my body, also on my head. In fact, most of all on the head. And it was mainly Todorovic who hit me in the back of my head. And I still have a crack in my skull which I can confirm with x-rays, and I have frequent headaches and consequences from this. Several times I had to spread my legs so that they could beat me in the crotch. And they would do this while saying that I wouldn't be needing it any more because we Muslims should not propagate. They also beat me on the back, all over my spine, and in the shins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a further question. During this beating taking such a long time, did you get unconscious in -- at any moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. I remember very clearly the last blow in the head inflicted by Stevan Todorovic, after which I fainted, because at that moment I lost consciousness and I remember my nose was bleeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: To follow up on that, Mr. Mehinovic, what did -- after these beatings to your head and your crotch and all over your body, in fact, what sort of injuries did you have after this particular beating?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I have injuries on my head. I have fractured ribs, two on the right side and one on the left. One of my fingers is broken, and a scar from a rifle butt on my index finger, and that blow was inflicted, one by Stevan Todorovic and another by Nikolic, in the course of the beating, which took a long time. Because the next day, when those three men had already been taken back, Nikolic, Todorovic, Goran, and I believe Sole too returned, and it was then that my index finger was injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, could I just concentrate on the first night that you were detained there just moment. Because I do appreciate that you went through many beatings, and I promise you, we will come to them in turn. That night when these men had finished beating you, could you just give us an idea of what you would have looked like? You mentioned your nose. Was your nose broken?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was, because to this day my nose is slightly twisted to the left. It was already late at night, and I could see in the window like in the mirror, and my neck was almost invisible to that extent. My head was swollen. It had almost merged with my shoulders. And I wasn't even allowed to lie down or sit down. I had to stand up every time the duty officer would come in. And regardless of the terrible pain I was in, I had to stand up in that intake room, despite the fact that my legs were very swollen. And I had also forgotten to say that after the beating was over, Mr. Stevan Todorovic ordered me to lick the bloodstains on the walls. He said he didn't want to see them any more in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have some of that blood on your clothing?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you then spend the night after this beating in that room by yourself?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was alone until the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I had wanted to ask you as well whether the three men who were brought in and also beaten with you at some time, were they of Muslim or Croat ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown one of the photographs from -- well, Your Honour, my colleague is pointing out to me that it is perhaps time for the break. Would it be appropriate to take the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the break now and continue at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has been informed that the Defence wanted to raise something before we continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you. Just very briefly. The basis of my submission is that -- first of all, I didn't want to interrupt the trial proceedings and the testimony of this witness. Basically, the Defence is of the opinion that up to now we heard enough evidence with regard to the acts of Stevan Todorovic, paramilitaries, members, and the other events in Samac, which are not directly related to the defendants here. In that respect - of course, it is at the discretion of this Trial Chamber - we would like to respectfully suggest that certain portions of the testimonies of this witness and coming witnesses, according to the approach of our learned friends from the Prosecution, would be avoided. Because, frankly - I'm speaking on behalf of my client - we could agree about the numerous facts related to Mr. Stevan Todorovic and paramilitaries, and it is the fact of common knowledge before this Trial Chamber that neither of us during our cross-examination challenged certain events and portions with regard to the detention, events in the SUP - I don't know - acts of police, et cetera. So basically, that would be our suggestion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber was actually looking at that point regarding -- looking at the cross-examination. Is it the submission of the Defence that they are not contesting any beatings by this witness and the rest of the witnesses to come?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking -- I'm speaking on behalf of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your client. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I can tell that we don't contest these acts of Todorovic's actions and certain members of paramilitary forces under his control. Of course, in certain stages of these proceedings we proceed with our cross-examinations with regard to the isolated parts of testimonies of certain witnesses where they mentioned my client in certain events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And successfully, I think, the Defence clarified that issue. So that is the position of Mr. Blagoje Simic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel of the same view, that they are not contesting the beatings? I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We might have that same position. I think it's very reasonable. I just haven't had a chance to discuss it with -- with our client. But I think it's a very reasonable --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Approach, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. I really do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In that case, then, you think that if you had an opportunity to discuss with your client, maybe you can have to -- you can come to some concessions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. What about Mr. Lukic? No concessions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I subscribe to what Mr. Pantelic has said as far as I understood him. My position and that of my client is that we cannot contest any right that we have to cross-examination if our clients are mentioned in similar incidents. But if we are speaking about incidents of beating involving third persons, we have no particular reason to dispute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Zaric has held this view from the very beginning, and we do not dispute the beatings. If perhaps a particular situation arose involving something out of the ordinary, perhaps that would be an exception. But we have heard so far so much evidence to this effect that this matter has become undisputed and incontestable, and to that extend we subscribe to the views expressed by our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pisarevic. I'm sure the Prosecution have understood what the Defence stand is.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, I -- I believe I partially -- myself and my colleague partially understand the position of the Defence. They no longer -- or are suggesting that it may no longer be necessary to lead evidence on the beatings because they concede that detainees were beaten -- or that Muslims and Croats were beaten. But may I just ask them to clarify exactly. Are they conceding that, for example, paragraph 15(C) of the indictment, that there was cruel and inhumane treatment of Bosnian Croats and Bosnian Muslims and other non-Serb civilians including beatings and torture and confinement under inhumane conditions? Are they conceding that they are not contesting that -- for example, that aspect of the persecutions charge existed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If we may, Your Honours. Of course, it is not our case. I mean, it's in very general terms. We are speaking about specific acts of Mr. Steven Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. On behalf of your client, that's what you're submitting. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we cannot accept this approach suggested by the Prosecution that in general terms we could say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean, that's a matter for the judgement of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Ms. Reidy, what this comes to is certainly not asking the witnesses for details of the -- how the beatings were done, the implements used and things like that. It will be sufficient for those witnesses who were not implicating any of the defendants in the beatings to simply discuss that they were beaten for so many days and so forth and so on, except where the implication -- the ones beating may be involving any of the accused. Then that's okay; you can go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will endeavour to do that. However, may I just make clear that our indictment, particularly, of course, with relation to Mr. Pantelic's client, is that Mr. Blagoje Simic himself was not often to be found in the police station beating people but he acted in concert with others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And we will show that indeed through the witness Mr. Todorovic when he comes to testify, how he worked with Mr. Todorovic and with the paramilitaries and others. So it's important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That part of the evidence is okay for the Prosecution to go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And we can also go into details -- I understand that they're conceding that Mr. Todorovic was -- engaged in acts of beating where there were other personnel who we believe -- who the Prosecution's case falls within the acting in concert with others. We would also like to have that evidence on record so that we can at the conclusion of the case prove beyond reasonable doubt that Mr. Blagoje Simic met the 7(1) requirements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is not being disputed, and the Prosecution can go into the details they need to meet the standard of proof.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I will endeavour to tailor my examination bearing the concessions of the Defence in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Usher, please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, briefly may I just update the Bench, perhaps before the witness comes in, on consultations between the Prosecution and Defence counsel for Milan Simic on the matter of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Simic has indicated to his counsel that what he would like is to be able to see a close-up picture on his monitor in the Detention Unit of the witness . Currently it's a broader picture. So if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So perhaps when the witness comes in, I'll instruct the audiovisual booth to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And then in the next break, Defence counsel can again consult Mr. Simic on his stance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Reidy, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps bearing in mind my recent intervention, the audiovisual booth could ensure that the witness is directly visible on the screen to Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I have just one or two more questions for you about this first night in the SUP. You said when you were -- when you were brought in that your possessions, including your watch, were taken from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So after you were initially brought into the SUP, your estimations on time are based on your observation rather than your ability to look at your watch or anything; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the beating which you described earlier involving bats and metal bars and that, the other three men - Mr. Dzakic, Cuba, and Mr. Hadzialijagic - they were subjected to similar treatment, were they, during this hour, hour and a half in the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I understand that you stayed in that room where you were first beaten for a number of days after that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you estimate roughly how many days you stayed in that particular room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Six to seven days. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I now ask the usher if photograph number 43 from Prosecution Exhibit 14 could be put on the ELMO for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Mehinovic, is this the building that -- sorry. I apologise. Mr. Mehinovic, is the building in the picture the building where you were held and subjected to the beating you described?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take the pointer and if you can, to the best of your recollection, indicate which of those rooms where you can see windows would be the one where you were first held and beaten.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: This window here by the small tree, right by the door. That was the window. That was that reception room.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know whether Mr. Zaric also had offices or operated from any of the other rooms in this building where you were?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was upstairs. I don't know in which room, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So according to your information, Mr. Zaric would have been in and around this building whilst you were held there for those six or seven days?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was there. I'm not sure. I only saw him that day when he let those people out.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But to your knowledge, he had an office in the same building?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with the photograph now.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, during these six or seven days in that room, did anyone else come and take this statement from you, the one that was the original pretext for bringing you to the building?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No. In those days, nobody asked for any statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did anyone come in and explain to you why you were being further detained?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did anyone come in and give you food or sustenance?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in that room.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you provided with blankets or mattresses, anything to sleep on in that room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you alone by yourself there for those six or seven days in that room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did anyone come to give you medical attention for the injuries you sustained in the first night's beating?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: During those six or seven days, did people come into your room to beat you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they come in every day or just once or twice during those six or seven days?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were the beatings similar in severity to the first night or did you sustain injuries from those beatings too?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was beaten as the first night. Whether they were all the same, whether the injuries were all the same, whether all the ribs were broken, I don't know, because I couldn't really tell from the pain, because my body was already numb.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So I take it you would be beaten on places where you had already sustained injury from the first night.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you allowed to visit the toilet or go to any place to have a wash or a shower?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I was only allowed to go to the toilet, but at that time there was no water, the city water supply system, but what we had to do was bring water from the well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many times a day would you be allowed to go to the toilet, or could you simply go when you wanted?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Only once in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you know of a person called Dadan Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Slobodan Jakupovic. Actually, Mr. Jakupovic isn't called Dadan. He is son of Irfu Travkar [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you hear whether anything happened to Mr. Slobodan Jakupovic whilst you were detained in this first room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. No, it wasn't Slobodan Jakupovic. It was Dadan Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's just a correction on the page 45, answer, line 3 until line 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
