utterances.text: Do you know how Mr. Seric came to have money with him whilst in the camp?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: After arriving at the Batkovici camp, after we all got together in the camp from SUP and other detainees from other locations, I heard from many friends of mine that Sabah Seric while he was still at Bosanski Samac was taken out and to his home. In other words, they were getting drunk together. This was no wonder that he at that time had some money with him, because there were no searches when we were taken to Batkovici from the other detention locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So when you witnessed this money change hands, did Mr. Tadic turn round there and then and tell you that you were no longer on the exchange list, or how did you learn that your name was now no longer on that list?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC
utterances.text: After the second call-out -- Mr. Tadic left after the first call-out to the warden of the camp. And in this -- and after this, in the second call-out, my name was no longer on the list. We had more freedom there. And I went to the commander to talk to him about that, but he said that unfortunately I had no money.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that the time is 7.00. Would you like me to halt my examination there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: First a question to Ms. Reidy. The document now having the number P54 and which you gave us a translation into English. As far as I can see, it is not dated. How about the original? Is there a date on the original document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the B/C/S itself has no date insofar as like a stamp or anything. But if you look at the preamble to the statement on the very first page, it's a paragraph written in the third person. And it says -- it describes the person giving the statement, Mr. Kemal Mehinovic. It describes who he was. And it says: "On the 7th of July, 1992, in the premises of Bosanski Samac --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Oh, there you find it. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You found it? Yes, the Prosecution submits that's the date it was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. But then I have a couple of questions to the witness. You told us that you were brought from one room to another and described it as a court. What gave you the impression that it was a court sitting behind the desk and a judge? And further, were you in any way interrogated during that occasion, and was there any kind of judgement given? What happened in that room when you stood there with one police officer on each side of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the very beginning, when I said that the police officer came to Batkovici and called my name to go to Bijeljina, I was told while I was entering the jeep that I was going to the court by this police officer. And then when I entered the second office, I only could assume that these were two judges, because there were two police officers, one on the left and one on the right of me. But nobody read any statements to me, nor was I -- was I given any kind of resolution. In Batkovici, I was given a decision that I was accused of armed -- insurgency that based on some article was punishable by the death penalty, based on the military laws in Bosnia-Herzegovina of the former Yugoslavia. Because at that time all legal matters were resolved based on the Yugoslav laws and not the Bosnian nor the laws of the Republika Srpska. They were using the legislature of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I may, with your permission, clarify my question. When you were staying there in what you call a courtroom, was there no interrogation and no judgement declared against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. I was never heard, nor was a judgement announced in that room. After the first words of that boss - I think he was a captain by rank - who asked me, "Do you know why you are here?" and I said, "No, I don't," all he said was, "You'll soon find out." That was the end of the conversation. There was nothing more that was said, nor did I know what was going to happen next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall rise and continue our proceedings tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
